extracted.intended_audience: news consumers, newsroom staff, and advocates/promoters of journalism trust standards (people sharing The Trust Project's Trust Indicators on social media)
extracted.subtask_short: promoting trust indicators on social media
extracted.subtask_description: Provide social-post-ready copy, explanations, and brief descriptions of The Trust Project's Trust Indicators so advocates, newsrooms, and readers can identify and share trustworthy journalism. The page highlights several of the individual indicators and gives sample social copy and sharing guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: The 8 Trust Indicators® (overall)
rubrics_metrics.description: The 8 Trust Indicators®, by The Trust Project®, empower us all to find information we can trust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Everyone deserves to know when they can trust news, especially when so much disinformation is pushing fear and divisiveness. Help share the 8 Trust Indicators far and wide; download social cards and language packets and link posts to https://thetrustproject.org/trust-indicators/. Use provided sample social posts and tag @TheTrustProject on Facebook, LinkedIn and Instagram.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Practices Trust Indicator®
rubrics_metrics.description: Truth is founded on high standards. The Best Practices Trust Indicator® helps you identify newsrooms that commit to clear ethics, accuracy and corrections so accountability is built into every story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sample social post text is provided for sharing; include CheckThe8 link (https://thetrustproject.org/trust-indicators/) and hashtags #Checkthe8 #TheTrustProject #Trustworthynews when posting to amplify recognition of newsrooms that follow best practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diverse Voices Trust Indicator®
rubrics_metrics.description: No single perspective tells the whole story. Use the Diverse Voices Trust Indicator® and look for reporting that reflects a range of voices and experiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating or sharing reporting, prefer stories that include a range of perspectives. Use the provided social copy and link to the Trust Indicators page to encourage others to look for diverse sources. Suggested hashtags: #Checkthe8 #TheTrustProject #Trustworthynews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Labels Trust Indicator®
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarity builds confidence. Use the Labels Trust Indicator® to look for a clear division of independently reported opinion and paid content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for explicit labeling that separates opinion, analysis, and sponsored/paid content from independently reported news. Share the Labels indicator with the provided sample text and link to explain how labeling supports trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods Trust Indicator®
rubrics_metrics.description: How was this story reported? Look for the Methods Trust Indicator®, where reporters explain their process so you can understand how information was gathered and verified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer reporting that transparently explains methods of information gathering and verification. When promoting trustworthy reporting, use the sample social text calling attention to Methods and link to the Trust Indicators page.

rubrics_metrics.name: NEWS consumer guidance (Never/Engage/Welcome/Share)
rubrics_metrics.description: As you go about your day, keep real NEWS in mind: Never share information without verifying its trustworthiness; Engage with trustworthy news sources and content; Welcome news from diverse reliable sources; Share the 8 Trust Indicators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This short mnemonic provides behavioral guidance for news consumers to reduce misinformation: always check for journalistic integrity before sharing, boost visibility of reliable information, seek multiple reputable sources for a full picture, and help others identify trustworthy journalism by sharing the Trust Indicators.
